findings.title: Missing input validation in version parsing
findings.description: The code splits the version string but does not truncate it. If a version string contains unexpected characters or an overly long pre-release identifier (e.g., '1.2.3.dev4+local'), the resulting list will have more than 3 elements. This can cause logical errors in subsequent version comparison or parsing logic within the `check_compatibility` function, potentially leading to incorrect compatibility checks or unhandled exceptions if the rest of the function assumes a specific length (like 3 parts). While not a direct vulnerability like injection, it represents an input validation weakness that could be exploited to cause Denial of Service (Crash) or bypass compatibility checks if the logic relies on the number of elements.
findings.suggestion: Truncate the split list to the first 3 elements to ensure consistent handling of the major, minor, and patch versions. Change the line to: `urllib3_version = urllib3_version.split(".")[:3]`. This matches the logic that follows which likely compares these three specific version components. Ensure robust input validation for the `urllib3_version` argument to handle non-standard version strings gracefully.
